findings.detail: Git resolves attributes per-attribute with the LAST matching line winning. `*      text=auto` is line 22, after `.apexyard/attestation.sig   -text` on line 20, so the `text` attribute for the signature resolves to `auto`, not unset — exactly what the comment on line 15 says it is preventing ("`-text` on the signature keeps git from touching it at all"). An SSHSIG file is armoured ASCII with no NULs, so auto-detection classifies it as text, and on checkout it is converted to the platform EOL (`core.eol` defaults to `native`; this checkout is on Windows). The sibling lines survive by accident: `.apexyard/attestation text eol=lf` keeps its `eol=lf` because line 22 does not set `eol`, only `text`. The failure is latent today because `.apexyard/allowed_signers` does not exist, but TD-028 commits to registering a key at the second-contributor trigger — at which point a CRLF'd `.sig` makes `ssh-keygen -Y verify` fail and `verify-evidence.mjs:337` reports "signature did not verify", which reads as tampering rather than as a checkout artifact.
findings.summary: `-text` on attestation.sig is inert — `* text=auto` on the last line overrides it

findings.detail: `const identity = signers.split('\n')[0].split(/\s+/)[0]` takes the principal from the first non-comment line, and that single value is passed to `ssh-keygen -Y verify -I`. `-I` asserts *which* principal is expected, so a signature made by the second registered key fails verification against the first principal — the check reports `signature did not verify for <someone-else@example.com>`, i.e. it names the wrong person and looks like tampering. This is precisely the configuration the feature exists for: `scripts/attest-review.mjs:181` and TD-028 both state the signature only becomes load-bearing "the moment a second contributor appears", which is the same moment `allowed_signers` gains a second line. Latent today (no signers file), which is why this is medium and not high.
findings.summary: Only the first identity in allowed_signers is ever used to verify the signature

findings.detail: `$RAW` is created (`mkdir -p`, line 160) but never cleared, and the guard at line 230 that suppresses bundle generation lists `SKIP_REVIEW`, `NOTHING_TO_PUSH`, and `REVIEW_QUALIFIED` — but not `SKIP_E2E`. So `npm run verify:local -- --skip-e2e` skips stage 5 and then runs stage 10, and `evidence.mjs` picks up the *previous* run's `.apexyard/raw/playwright.json` and `test-results/axe-summary.*.json`. `collectPlaywright` and `collectAccessibility` see non-null input and emit `available: true` with `passed_count`/`violations_total` describing a run that never happened against this code. That is the one property `collectors.mjs:5-9` is built to guarantee ("'0 failures' and 'never ran' look identical in a summary table and mean opposite things") — defeated one layer up, in a committed artifact, with no verifier able to notice because CI deliberately does not regenerate. The same staleness applies in a full run if the Playwright stage dies before its reporter writes. The exit-2 "NOT a valid pre-push state" message warns the human but does not stop the bundle from being rewritten on disk, which is why this is medium rather than low.
findings.summary: `--skip-e2e` regenerates the bundle from the previous run's raw output

findings.detail: `walkSources` reads the filesystem and only excludes `SKIP_DIR` plus dotfiles, so any untracked or newly-gitignored `.ts`/`.tsx` file on the maintainer's machine is counted in `source_files`, `total_loc`, `by_directory`, and possibly `oversized.files` of the committed `architecture.json`. The artifact then describes a repository state that does not exist in git, and nothing can detect it: `evidence.mjs --check` regenerates from the same tree so it agrees, and CI deliberately does not regenerate (ci.yml:262-265). For an artifact whose stated contract is byte-reproducibility from the reviewed content, deriving its inputs from the tree rather than the index is the wrong source.
findings.summary: collectArchitecture walks the working tree, so untracked files enter a committed artifact

findings.detail: `const ID = att.digest` takes the digest straight from the header, and that value is then stamped into all seven artifacts as `attestation_id`. `parseAttestation` does not check the digest against the body — `verify-evidence.mjs:143` does, and `scripts/lib/attestation.mjs:276` exports `verifyDigest` for exactly this purpose. If the manifest is ever hand-edited or half-written, `npm run evidence` happily produces a fully self-consistent bundle bound to an id no verifier will accept, and the real reason ("attestation digest does not match its body") surfaces later from a different script. Impact is small because stage 11 runs the verifier moments later; the cost of fixing is two lines.
findings.summary: The generator trusts the manifest's digest line without rehashing the body

findings.detail: Carried over — recorded in the previous round's `findings.json` and still present. `json.filter(...).map((f) => toPosixRelative(f.filePath, root)).sort().length` computes POSIX-relative paths for every ESLint file with findings, sorts them, and keeps only the count. The mapping and the deterministic sort only make sense if the *list* was meant to be emitted, so the shape reads as an editing casualty rather than a choice, and `root` is threaded into `collectEslint` for no observable effect. The docblock on line 122 ("file paths made relative") describes output the payload does not contain.
findings.summary: files_with_findings maps and sorts an array only to discard it and take .length

findings.detail: Carried over — recorded in the previous round and still present. I re-grepped the repo: nothing imports these. `scripts/evidence.mjs:36-40` imports only the `collect*` functions and `SEVERITY_ORDER`; `tests/unit/evidence.test.ts` imports neither; and `collectors.d.mts` does not declare them, so a TypeScript caller could not use them anyway. `readJson` (line 24) is unreferenced inside the module too — every collector takes already-parsed JSON — and `statSync` exists only to be re-exported. Re-exporting `node:fs` from a domain module also blurs the boundary: a future caller could reach `fs` through `collectors.mjs`.
findings.summary: Dead export: readJson, existsSync, and statSync have no consumer

findings.detail: Carried over — recorded in the previous round and still present. Lines 98-109 explain, correctly and with the verification, that this file is deliberately *in* its own sweep (every pattern's literal text has a `[` immediately after the prefix, which is outside each character class, so none self-match). Two leftover comments from the previous behaviour say the opposite: lines 128-129 ("Skipping this file is not cosmetic: it necessarily contains every pattern it searches for, so including it guarantees a self-match") and line 153 ("Skipping the pattern-list lines themselves, now that the file is in scope"). Neither describes any code — `list_scan_targets` has no exclusion and the loop has no filter. In a security script this is worse than ordinary comment rot: the surviving comment asserts a self-match is guaranteed, which invites the next maintainer to re-add the exclusion and reintroduce the blind spot lines 98-109 were written to close.
findings.summary: Stale comments claim the scanner skips itself, contradicting the code above them

findings.detail: Carried over — recorded in the previous round and still present. The comment added at lines 19-21 states "No baseUrl: it is deprecated in TS 6 and removed in 7" and explains that `paths` resolves relative to the config file when baseUrl is absent — but line 18 sets `"baseUrl": "."`, and the pre-existing TD-001 comment immediately above (lines 15-17) explains why the alias block is needed. Two adjacent comments now contradict each other, and one contradicts the config it annotates. The next reader either deletes a setting the TD-001 note implies is load-bearing, or spends time working out which comment is stale. No runtime impact today: `baseUrl: "."` and an absent baseUrl resolve `./node_modules/@e965/xlsx` identically from the repo root.
findings.summary: New comment says "No baseUrl" directly below `"baseUrl": "."`
